pairs.question: Martine, quid dubitas credere, cum videas? Christus ego sum.
pairs.answer: Non se Iesus Dominus purpuratum nec diademate renidentem venturum esse praedixit: ego Christum nisi in eo habitu formaque, qua passus est, nisi crucis stigmata praeferentem venisse non credam.
pairs.derivation: The devil, disguised as Christ in royal regalia, directly asks Martin why he hesitates to believe. The question is the devil's whole quoted utterance ('Martine, quid dubitas credere, cum videas? Christus ego sum'). Martin's reply genuinely answers the 'why': he states why he will not believe. I drop the speech-tag framing ('tum ille, revelante sibi spiritu, ut intellegeret diabolum esse, non Dominum; ... inquit ...') and normalized the opening capitalization. The answer ends at the close of Martin's utterance, before the narration 'ad hanc ille vocem statim ut fumus evanuit'. No interior ellipsis; the two answer sentences are contiguous in the source.
